events.title: Germany: Bundeswehr troop numbers reach 13-year high

events.summary: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

events.title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football

events.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?
events.summary: Russia has become one of the world's biggest sellers of gold over the past 12 months. It's an attempt to raise cash in the face of budget issues, but not necessarily a sign of a looming financial crisis.

events.title: The hidden problem with small modular nuclear reactors
events.summary: Mini nuclear reactors are seen as a flexible energy source. Their promise: abundant energy, cheap, clean and climate-friendly with lower water use. But do the numbers add up? We look at what's behind the SMR hype.

events.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep
events.summary: Every so often we hear of high-ranking politicians or CEOs claiming to get by on very little sleep — some as little as three hours a night. If they're not natural short sleepers, chances are they're heading for trouble.

events.title: AI ecosystem's 'circular' investment: risk or advantage?
events.summary: Amid talk of an AI sector bubble, one aspect is under scrutiny. Many big AI players are invested in smaller ones, who then buy the bigger firm's products. This brings risks and advantages.

events.title: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
events.summary: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy
events.summary: The world number one women's tennis player supports the WTA's new sex testing rules. Others are more critical of the policy.

events.title: G20 backs final statement despite Russia tensions, China dissent
events.summary: G20 finance leaders wrapped up two days of talks in Ashville, North Carolina, on Tuesday with broad backing for a final statement, despite tensions over Russia’s participation and divisions with China. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Moscow’s presence had not disrupted discussions, as ministers also grappled with the war in the Middle East, tariffs, global trade imbalances and continued support for Ukraine.

events.title: "Subtle changes pointing to consumer fatigue" a challenge for fast-fashion retailers, expert says
events.summary: A federation of European textile associations called Tuesday for an import fee of 10 euros on fashion imports, the latest effort to stem the flood of ultra-cheap competition mainly from China. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Dr Sheng Lu, Professor at the Department of Fashion and Apparel Studies at the University of Delaware, says that it remains to be seen just "to what extent such measures would push groups like Shein to change their business model", adding that fast-fashion retailers may have to start to contend with "consumer fatigue".

events.title: Germany blames Russia for airport drone incident, hits back with sanctions
events.summary: Germany on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted "hybrid attack" involving an explosive-laden drone at a strategic airport last month and announced diplomatic counter-measures. The European Union expressed "full solidarity" with Germany, NATO assured that it would defend its members and countries including Britain, Estonia and Poland offered strong backing. Germany will close Russia's consulate in the former capital Bonn later this month, and cancel the contract for the Russian House, a cultural centre in Berlin, said Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

events.title: Global bond selloff deepens as US launches fresh attacks on Iran
events.summary: Oil prices rose, stocks fell and bond yields spiked after the US launched fresh attacks on Iranian targets. Japan's 10-year bond yield hit 3% for the first time since 1996.  The deepening global selloff comes amid fears over rising inflation and concern over mounting government debt - which in the US has risen above 40 trillion dollars. Meanwhile, in the single-currency Eurozone, inflation rose to the highest level in three years in August, driven by higher energy prices.

events.title: Burnham pledges to restore hope as he makes his House of Commons debut as UK leader
events.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced lawmakers in the House of Commons on Tuesday for the first time since becoming U.K. leader six weeks ago, with wars in Europe and the Middle East weighing on his promise to kick-start the economy, ease the cost of living and oversee a radical redistribution of power from London to Britain's regions. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Martin Farr, Senior Lecturer in British Contemporary History at Newcastle University.

events.title: Football: Europe's top clubs scramble for last-minute signings
events.summary: The football transfer window is entering its final hours. After a lot of last-minute negotiations, Manchester City are reported to have reached an agreement with Chelsea to sign Argentinian midfielder Enzo Fernandez for 125 million pounds – the biggest fee in a 3.3 billion euro spending frenzy by the top clubs. Meanwhile Aston Villa have signed 18-year-old winger Ibrahim Mbaye from PSG for 55 million euros.

events.title: South Africans missing in Nepal's glacial flood
events.summary: In tonight's edition, Africa Disaster Relief is looking for 6 South Africans who went missing in the deadly floods on the border  between Nepal and China. Also, South African illegal miners are undermining their own communities. And rising fuel prices are pushing Kenyans' shifts to electric vehicles.

events.title: Google Maps changes Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’ as MapQuest downloads surge
events.summary: Lake Ontario is now appearing as “Lake America” on Google Maps for US users, following Donald Trump’s executive order to rename the lake. Canadians still see “Lake Ontario”, while users elsewhere see both names. But the change is far from universal: Apple Maps and MapQuest continue to use Lake Ontario. MapQuest has remained defiant against the move and since surged to the top of the US App Store download charts.

events.title: AI data centers become surprise issue in US midterm elections
events.summary: The boom of data centers to power artificial intelligence was a topic of discussion at the G20 summit on Tuesday in North Carolina. Elon Musk told member countries that US companies need to find new energy sources outside of China to power these massive data centers. That same issue is also creating a backlash in the United States ahead of the midterm elections in November. Donald Trump is doubling down, calling those who are against the data centers, “backwards and poor.” FRANCE 24's Monte Francis explains.

events.title: US firm to take over some Venezuela oilfields previously run by Chinese, Russian firms
events.summary: The White House on Monday said it’s partnering with North American Blue Energy Partners as part of President Donald Trump’s push to tap into Venezuela’s oil industry, setting up a deal that will give the Pentagon a stake over roughly a fifth of the country’s vast oil reserves. Venezuela's ruling party-dominated ​National Assembly backed the ​country's oil deal with the Trump administration in a vote on ​Tuesday. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

events.title: Mass burials held in Nepal as bodies wash up after catastrophic flooding
events.summary: Every day, new bodies are recovered in Nepal, but many remain unidentifiable. Several days after the disaster, some are already in an advanced state of decomposition. Morgues in the country's main cities are reaching capacity. Faced with the influx of remains, authorities have begun burying them without formal identification. France 24's special correspondents traveled to Bharatpur, in southern Nepal, to one of these burial sites.

events.title: School without screens: Will France's high school phone ban fly?
events.summary: A lot happened during summer recess: France’s constitutional council struck down the core of a new law to ban social media for under 15 year olds, but it did validate the extension to high schoolers of a phone ban already in effect for younger pupils. Why one but not the other? On this the first day of school across this country and others, we’ll size up what's best for future citizens, parents and teachers… all grappling in this age of distraction with the lure of screens.

events.title: US and Iran trade fire as hostilities flare again
events.summary: The US military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday as Tehran reponded with retaliatory strikes as hostilities between the two countries flared once again in an intermittent war that has lasted more than six months. One US strike hit a home hosting a wedding, killing four people and wounding dozens, local officials said.

events.title: Lindsay Clancy: The trial putting postpartum mental illness in the spotlight
events.summary: Jurors in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy notified the judge ​on September 1 that they were unable to reach a unanimous decision on whether to convict her for killing her three young children at her home in ​2023 – a ‌tragedy her attorney contends occurred while she was suffering ⁠from postpartum psychosis. FRANCE 24 takes a closer look at this case, which has sparked fevered debate in the United States over postpartum mental health.

events.title: Germany blames Russia for Leipzig airport drone attack, orders Russian consulate closed
events.summary: Germany's government on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport on 4 August using an explosive-laden drone, and announced that it would shut down a Russian consulate among other measures against Moscow. French ​President Emmanuel Macron ​said he supported the ​adoption ‌of ⁠new European sanctions ‌against Russia after the attempted drone attack.

events.title: What to know about the new UK PM's agenda as he faces lawmakers
events.summary: Since taking office on July 20, Burnham has traveled around the country promising to deliver renewed national optimism after the downbeat two-year tenure of his predecessor Keir Starmer. Now, it's time for him to face lawmakers for the first time since he has taken office after an unusually long time without having to do so due to the summer recess. FRANCE 24's Benedicte Paviot tells us what to know from his speech.

events.title: Germany set to blame Russia for airport explosive-laden drone incident
events.summary: Berlin is set to formally blame Russia for an incident involving drones at a strategic airport on the night of August 4-5, including one that was found carrying explosives. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt are expected to accuse a Russian intelligence service of being behind the incident. It would be the first time Germany formally blames Moscow for an incident like this one.

events.title: Replay: UK PM Andy Burnham faces lawmakers for first time since taking office

events.title: Niger's thwarted mutiny highlights junta's dependence on Russia

They argue that the failed mutiny on Saturday shows how the country's security landscape has worsened and contradicts claims from Niger's junta about the country's independence from foreign powers.

events.title: From North Korea to ICE: Photojournalist David Guttenfelder on the front lines in Minneapolis
events.summary: David Guttenfelder from The New York Times has spent 35 years photographing history around the world. Now, he is documenting it at home. The award-winning photojournalist is known for his work in Rwanda, North Korea and conflict zones across the globe. This year, he turned his camera on Minneapolis, documenting the federal immigration crackdown and deadly clashes involving ICE. His exhibition "The People of Minneapolis vs. ICE" is currently on show at the Visa pour l'Image photojournalism festival in Perpignan.

events.title: After 'unprecedented honeymoon', UK PM faces lawmakers for first time
events.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will face lawmakers in the House of Commons on September 1 for the first time since becoming UK leader six weeks ago. This comes as the wars in Europe and the Middle East weighing on his promise to kick-start the economy and ease the cost of living. Andy Burnham has enjoyed quite a long time without facing lawmakers due to the summer recess. FRANCE 24's Benedicte Paviot tells us more.

events.title: Alejandro Betancourt, the controversial Venezuelan oil tycoon Trump is banking on

Washington is set to take a 35 percent stake in North American Blue Energy Partners, which is owned by controversial Venezuelan oil tycoon Alejandro Betancourt.

events.title: At least 12 killed and over a dozen injured in Russian strikes on Kyiv

events.summary: A day after Davis was found guilty of first-degree murder, his attorney told NBC News the defense had been preparing for an appeal before the trial even began.

events.title: Alaska finalizes Senate race for November: 3 Republicans — 2 Dans Sullivan — and 1 Democrat
events.summary: Former Rep. Mary Peltola will be the only Democrat on the ballot after Democrat David Leslie, who finished fourth in the primary, withdrew.

events.title: House censures GOP Rep. Chuck Edwards over ‘inappropriate conduct’ with female staffers
events.summary: A bipartisan ethics probe found Edwards, R-N.C., showered the aides with lavish gifts, invited them to intimate dinners and trips and wrote them poetry. He denied any wrongdoing.

events.title: Student who felt ‘humiliated’ by ICE ankle monitor dies by suicide
events.summary: Pierre Damas Bel, 20, expressed feeling “shame and humiliation” at having to wear by an ankle monitor. The college student died by suicide days later.

events.title: What to watch in Massachusetts: From the Politics Desk
events.summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

events.title: No plans for ICE to be at polls for midterms, DHS says
events.summary: A senior DHS official said ICE will do its regular duties on the day of midterm elections, though Secretary Markwayne Mullin said agents would enter a polling place to serve a warrant.

events.title: When is it safe to return home after a wildfire? California becomes first state to pass standards
events.summary: California is poised to become the first U.S. state to set standards for testing and remediation for smoke contamination from wildfires, with a pair of bills passed Monday.

events.title: Nepal flood deaths pass 1,000 as hope fades in the search for survivors
events.summary: The overwhelming stench of death is crushing hopes that more survivors will be found in this Nepali town devastated by last week’s catastrophic floods.

events.title: U.S. has launched ‘large and powerful’ strikes on Iran, Trump says
events.summary: The strikes were in “retaliation for the Iranians’ failed attempt at adding sea mines” in the Strait of Hormuz, Trump said on Truth Social.

events.title: Tracking U.S., state and county gas prices, in maps and charts
events.summary: Are gas prices declining? NBC News is tracking national, state and county prices at the pump.

events.title: United States and Iran trade strikes for the first time in a month
events.summary: Iran launched retaliatory missiles toward Jordan, a U.S. ally, but they were intercepted by American forces, a source said.

events.title: U.S. strikes targets in Iran near Strait of Hormuz as Iran says it is retaliating
events.summary: President Trump said that the U.S. launched “large and powerful” strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command said that it had targeted “Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran.”  In response, Iran’s armed forces general staff said that it would retaliate. NBC News' Keir Simmons reports.

events.title: Thai police crackdown on sex workers ahead of USS Lincoln’s arrival
events.summary: Police in Pattaya, Thailand, are intensifying a crackdown on sex workers ahead of the arrival of the USS Lincoln after the aircraft carrier’s lengthy deployment in the Middle East. While prostitution is illegal in Thailand, sex workers often operate openly in major tourist hubs like Bangkok and Pattaya.

events.title: Nepali principal saves 900 lives as deadly floods approached
events.summary: Rajendra Dawadi, the principal of a school in Nepal’s Trishuli Valley, describes the moment he evacuated his school before the floods hit, saving the lives of 900 people.

events.title: Women and girls take virtual classes to get around severe restrictions on education in Afghanistan
events.summary: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghan women continue pushing back against severe restrictions placed on them, including bans on education. NBC News' Daniele Hamadjian speaks with a few who are finding new ways to bypass those laws.

events.title: Send your questions for Richard Engel on Ukraine and more
events.summary: Richard Engel is back in Ukraine to report on its intensifying war with Russia, with a strike this weekend on a warehouse west of Kyiv becoming its deadliest attack this year — more than 38 people were killed.

events.title: Allies bristle as sanctioned Russian finance minister attends U.S.-hosted G20 summit
events.summary: Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov was left out of the “family photo” of finance ministers at a G20 meeting after complaints from Ukraine’s allies.

events.title: Record baby boom brings world’s heaviest parrot back from the brink
events.summary: A record 90 chicks have been added to the population count of the kakapo parrot in New Zealand, delighting conservationists.

events.title: Thieves steal royal necklace from Vienna museum in smash-and-grab heist
events.summary: The robbers, who didn’t disguise their faces and were caught on camera, remain at large with the 673-diamond necklace once owned by an Egyptian queen, police said.

events.title: Death toll in Nepal floods tops 900; number of missing nearly doubles to more than 4,200
events.summary: Rescuers continue to struggle to reach communities days after the massive flooding that stemmed from a glacier collapse.

events.title: Bootleg ‘Spider-Man’ swings into Russian cinemas despite Hollywood boycott
events.summary: While screening the movie “violates both Russian and international law,” everyone, including Russian authorities, “turns a blind eye to it,” one film critic told NBC News.

events.title: Sen. Ted Cruz calls for elections in Venezuela to proceed ‘rapidly’
events.summary: The Texas Republican also said the U.S. should arm protesters in Iran.

events.title: Fears of more flooding in Nepal, 100 Americans among the missing as rescue efforts step up
events.summary: Nepal’s Flood Alert system warned heavy rain could raise water levels in some areas, prompting fresh alerts for residents along waterways.

events.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to more than 700 as nearly 2,500 remain missing
events.summary: The death toll from catastrophic flash floods and mudslides in Nepal rose to at least 734 on Saturday, as nearly 2,500 people remained missing in the country, including about 100 Americans.

events.title: Palestinian woman and NBC News team attacked by masked Israeli settlers in West Bank
events.summary: The woman and the crew were treated for injuries. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence committed “by a handful of rioters.”

events.title: Trump says U.S. has struck deal with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves
events.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that the U.S. had entered into an agreement with Venezuela to take control of the country’s 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.

events.title: Families wait in agony as Nepal floods leave hundreds missing
events.summary: A New York couple traveling to Mount Kailash is among 65 Americans missing after a catastrophic flood along the Nepal-Tibet border.

events.title: Harry and Meghan arrive for ‘extended’ stay in the U.K. six years after royal exit
events.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan arrived back in the U.K.  after six years in California, a source close to the family confirmed to NBC News.

events.title: Hundreds are missing after catastrophic flooding in Nepal wipes out whole towns
events.summary: Flash floods hit Himalayan mountain towns and villages, sweeping away vehicles, bridges and even buildings as people fled in terror.

events.title: Iran vows retaliation after U.S. widens sanctions, fueling fears of escalated war
events.summary: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran has vowed to retaliate against widened U.S. sanctions, saying Washington should “expect an attack” in response.
